children: Converse is reviewing its internal approval procedures after an advertisement drew widespread criticism for imagery that some viewers associated with the Ku Klux Klan and lynching, Bloomberg News reported Sunday.
Chief Executive Aaron Cain told employees that the Nike-owned
brand removed the images after concerns surfaced and is examining how the campaign passed its review process. He said management would make changes intended to prevent similar incidents.

The disputed image, part of a Chuck 70 X campaign, showed a person in a white garment holding a pair of shoes. Critics on social media said shadows made the clothing resemble a KKK hood, while the placement of the shoes suggested a hanging.
Converse previously withdrew the advertisement and issued a public apology. Cain did not specify what changes the company may make.
For investors, the controversy adds another challenge to Nike’s

effort to revive Converse, which has posted 13 consecutive quarters of declining revenue. The backlash could further weaken demand, complicate marketing and delay a turnaround at one of Nike’s most persistently troubled businesses.

title: Converse reviews ad approvals after campaign draws racism backlash
